correctness.rationale: The assumptions imply replication r=(v-1)/(k-1), MM^T=(r-1)I+J, and point Schur complement (vI-J)/k. For every source incidence (p0,B0), the exact mean-zero point potential is (k/v)e_p0-(1/v)1_B0, with the block potential obtained by dividing M^T x - e_B0 by k. Pair uniqueness gives exactly six nonzero edge-current types; their counts sum to R+5(k-1)(v-k)/(vk), with R=1/k+(k-1)/v in (0,1). The canonical cut projection therefore has l1 norm 5-4/k-4(k-1)/v and its complement 6-6/k-6(k-1)/v. Because the source incidence was arbitrary and projections symmetric, every column has the same sum and l_infinity norm equals l1. The checker independently reconstructs six graphs and all 357 exact rational columns, with symbolic count and formula identities. Finite tests are supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic research searches, comparison to the full 2023 graph-projection article, full public Steiner-design incidence-graph result, and an affine-plane graph paper did not identify the two exact all-design endpoint-norm formulas or the sharp dominance locus. The existing general graph Schur-complement identity is method, not coverage: the particular signs and complete absolute current counts require the Steiner unique-pair condition. Generalized-polygon formulas imply the projective-plane subfamily but not all Steiner 2-designs; higher design regularity and symmetric-design assumptions cannot subsume an arbitrary Steiner system. Residual risk is an equivalent earlier electrical-network calculation under alternate nomenclature.

value.rationale: Steiner 2-design incidence graphs form a substantial, structurally natural class with many nonisomorphic realizations and no required edge-transitive symmetry. A pairwise-uniqueness combinatorial axiom unexpectedly forces exact universal endpoint Banach projection norms depending solely on the two design parameters, including many non-symmetric triple systems and affine planes. The complementary norms exchange dominance exactly at (k-2)v=2k(k-1), giving a sharp classification with nontrivial instances on both sides, including all existing Steiner triple systems of orders 7 and 9 versus those of order at least 13. These are exact operator invariants directly motivated by transportation-cost projection problems; no unrelated finite slice or arbitrary parameter is selected.
